flashcards.definition: The amount of substance containing $$6.022\times10^{23}$$ representative particles; it connects particle counts to measurable laboratory masses.
A constant equal to $$6.022\times10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}$$ used to convert between amount in moles and number of particles.
The mass of one mole of a substance, expressed in $$\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$$, calculated by summing the atomic masses in its chemical formula.
The percent by mass of each element in a compound, determined from the element’s total mass contribution divided by the compound’s molar mass and multiplied by $$100\%$$.
An analytical technique that separates ions based on their mass-to-charge ratios and provides isotope masses and relative abundances.

multipleChoice.questionText: A sample contains $$1.50\ \mathrm{mol}$$ of $$\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$$. How many oxygen atoms are present in the sample?
What is the percent by mass of oxygen in $$\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$$? Use atomic masses $$\mathrm{Na}=22.99$$, $$\mathrm{S}=32.06$$, and $$\mathrm{O}=16.00$$.

fillInTheBlank.questionText: To convert a measured mass of $$\mathrm{CO_2}$$ in grams to the number of $$\mathrm{CO_2}$$ molecules, one should ______.
options: multiply by the molar mass of $$\mathrm{CO_2}$$ and divide by $$N_A$$
divide by the molar mass of $$\mathrm{CO_2}$$ and multiply by $$N_A$$
divide by $$44.01\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$$ and divide by $$N_A$$
multiply by $$44.01\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$$ and multiply by $$N_A$$
fillInTheBlank.correctAnswer: divide by the molar mass of $$\mathrm{CO_2}$$ and multiply by $$N_A$$

fillInTheBlank.questionText: The atomic mass listed on the periodic table is best described as ______.
options: the mass of the most abundant isotope only
the arithmetic mean of the mass numbers of all isotopes
the weighted average of naturally occurring isotopes
the sum of all isotope masses multiplied by $$100$$
fillInTheBlank.correctAnswer: the weighted average of naturally occurring isotopes

flashcards.definition: The arrangement of electrons among orbitals in an atom or ion, written using energy levels, subshells, and superscripts to show occupancy.
The rule stating that electrons occupy lower-energy orbitals before higher-energy orbitals in the ground state.
The rule stating that electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before pairing occurs.
The net positive attraction experienced by an electron in a multielectron atom after accounting for shielding by other electrons.
The minimum energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom or ion in its ground state.

multipleChoice.questionText: Which electron configuration is correct for $$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$$ in its ground state?
Among $$\mathrm{Na}$$, $$\mathrm{Mg}$$, $$\mathrm{Al}$$, and $$\mathrm{Si}$$, which element has the greatest second ionization energy, and why?
options: $$\mathrm{Na}$$, because its valence electron is in a higher principal energy level
$$\mathrm{Mg}$$, because removing the second electron produces a stable noble-gas configuration
$$\mathrm{Al}$$, because its first electron removed is from a $$3p$$ orbital
$$\mathrm{Si}$$, because it has the greatest effective nuclear charge in the set
multipleChoice.correctAnswer: $$\mathrm{Mg}$$, because removing the second electron produces a stable noble-gas configuration

fillInTheBlank.questionText: In a photoelectron spectrum, a peak at lower binding energy corresponds to electrons that are ______.
options: lower energy and closer to the nucleus
higher energy and farther from the nucleus
higher nuclear charge with no additional shielding
lower shielding and smaller atomic radius
fillInTheBlank.correctAnswer: higher energy and farther from the nucleus

fillInTheBlank.questionText: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally decreases because ______.
options: principal energy level decreases
effective nuclear charge increases
valence electrons experience more shielding by electrons in the same shell
nuclear charge decreases
